head: 97269b60617c3c614440df08702c6adf2343040c
summary: Three added comments require correction or human resolution; the diff is otherwise comment-only.  |  Several Range comments omit its overfull-range failure mode or promise iterator behavior the implementation does not provide; one unresolved NEEDS-HUMAN note remains public.  |  Several added docs overstate generic type relationships or omit a material forcing behavior.  |  Two added comments are materially inaccurate or unresolved; the remaining diff is comment-only.  |  The added conversion docs systematically omit explicit-null behavior, and the `Properties` doc also hides material view limitations.  |  Two concurrent-map method docs incorrectly promise atomic Java default-method behavior; several return-value docs also miss required tags.  |  Three added Scaladoc comments retain unresolved NEEDS-HUMAN findings; all diff additions are comment-only.  |  The added Scaladoc matches the implementations; only minor consistency and formatting issues remain.

items.issue: NEEDS-HUMAN: the implementation passes `start.id` directly to a bit set whose ids are offset by `bottomId`; the JVM implementation passes `start.id - bottomId`. Is this Scala.js behavior intentional for enumerations with negative ids?
items.suggestion: Resolve the platform-behavior question before merge; either fix the implementation or revise the documented contract and remove the NEEDS-HUMAN marker.

items.issue: The `@throws IllegalArgumentException` documentation omits the exception raised for insufficient `BigDecimal` precision. `NumericRange.count` calls `bigDecimalCheckUnderflow`, which throws `IllegalArgumentException` when the endpoints cannot represent the requested step accurately.
items.suggestion: Include inadequate `BigDecimal` precision as an `IllegalArgumentException` condition, or describe the delegated validation comprehensively.

items.issue: The documented exception condition is too narrow. A signed fixed-width type can also throw when negating the minimum step overflows and leaves its sign unchanged, e.g. a `Long` range with `step == Long.MinValue`.
items.suggestion: State that `ArithmeticException` is thrown whenever negating `step` does not change its sign, including signed-integer overflow, rather than attributing it only to unsigned element types.

items.issue: The method evaluates `length` while constructing the stepper, so it throws `IllegalArgumentException` for ranges with more than `Int.MaxValue` elements; the documentation presents unconditional successful construction.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws IllegalArgumentException` tag for overfull ranges.

items.issue: Using the default `end` evaluates `length - 1`, which throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an overfull range. The documented unconditional result is therefore false when the default is used.
items.suggestion: Document the `IllegalArgumentException` condition for the default argument, or otherwise qualify the result description.

items.issue: The Range-vs-Range branch immediately reads `this.length` and can throw `IllegalArgumentException` for an overfull range, rather than returning the documented comparison result.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws IllegalArgumentException` tag for comparisons requiring an overfull range's length.

items.issue: With the standard `Int` numeric, `size` delegates to `length`; an overfull range throws `IllegalArgumentException` instead of returning the stated sum.
items.suggestion: Add the type-dependent `IllegalArgumentException` case to the documentation.

items.issue: The returned iterators call `Range.this.length` from `hasNext`, so consuming either iterator throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an overfull range instead of yielding all documented tails or inits.
items.suggestion: Document that traversing the returned iterator fails for ranges with more than `Int.MaxValue` elements.

items.issue: For a non-empty overfull range, the returned iterator's `hasNext` calls `length` and throws `IllegalArgumentException`; it does not provide the documented groups.
items.suggestion: Add the overfull-range failure case to the documentation of the returned iterator.

items.issue: `end` is documented as an "exclusive upper bound", but descending ranges use a negative step and have `end` as their lower bound.
items.suggestion: Call `end` the exclusive end boundary rather than an upper bound.

items.issue: It does not reliably return the number of remaining elements: `(lastElement - _next)` is evaluated as an `Int` and overflows for some large ranges.
items.suggestion: Do not promise an accurate remaining count unless the underlying implementation is fixed; otherwise document the overflow limitation.

items.issue: The claim that it skips the next `n` elements is false for overflowing `step * n`, which is multiplied as `Int` before being assigned to `longPos`.
items.suggestion: Remove or qualify the unconditional behavior claim; ideally fix the calculation to multiply in `Long` outside this comment-only PR.

items.issue: NEEDS-HUMAN: Is the JavaScript-only equality implementation, including equality of distinct builders whose current `elems` fields are both `null`, intentionally allowed to have no corresponding `hashCode` override and to differ from the JVM variant?
items.suggestion: Resolve the question with a maintainer, then remove the public `@note NEEDS-HUMAN` marker and document only the settled contract.

items.issue: The `xs` tag says its elements are counted, but the implementation never reads `xs`; only `length` changes the count.
items.suggestion: Describe `xs` as the ignored source array.

items.issue: "Current number of elements." is a fragment that only restates the identifier.
items.suggestion: Use a complete summary with meaningful builder-specific information, or omit this redundant comment.

items.issue: The extractor calls `s.tail`; a non-empty `Stream` evaluates its tail expression on that call. The comment singles out only the head as evaluated, omitting this material eager evaluation.
items.suggestion: State that extracting a `Stream` also evaluates its tail expression, or remove the evaluation claim.

items.issue: `T` is not checked against `runtimeClass1`: for example, `ClassTag[String](classOf[Int])` returns the shared `Int` tag cast to `ClassTag[String]`. The `@tparam` claims that `T` is the type whose erasure is the supplied class.
items.suggestion: Document the caller obligation to supply a runtime class compatible with `T`, rather than presenting that relation as guaranteed.

items.issue: The added documentation claims that `arg` manifests element type `T`, but `arg` is `Manifest[_]` and the implementation delegates to a cast-based factory. A caller can choose a mismatched `T`, yielding a manifest whose represented element type does not match its static result type.
items.suggestion: Document that callers must ensure `arg` represents `T`; apply the same correction to the identical added documentation on `ManifestFactory.arrayType`.

items.issue: The added `@note NEEDS-HUMAN` identifies an unresolved mismatch: the declaration and cast target are `java.lang.Boolean`, while the documentation describes boxing a `Byte`. What is the intended signature and behavior?
items.suggestion: Resolve the underlying intended API with a maintainer, then document the confirmed behavior and remove the NEEDS-HUMAN marker.

items.issue: The summary claims `atLevel` is a minimum dimension count, but for `atLevel <= 0` the implementation recurses until it reaches a non-array component and returns `false`; even an array therefore does not satisfy the stated "at least 0 dimensions" behavior.
items.suggestion: Document the actual behavior for non-positive `atLevel`, or explicitly limit the documented contract to positive values without claiming an unenforced general minimum.

items.issue: The comment describes the `MatchError` for a non-array only in prose, contrary to the exception-tag convention.
items.suggestion: Add `@throws MatchError if xs is not an array` (in addition to the existing NullPointerException tag).

items.issue: The summary begins with “Copies” and the comment omits an `@return`, so the returned `Array[AnyRef]` and primitive boxing guarantee are not presented in a return tag.
items.suggestion: Add an `@return` describing the new `Array[AnyRef]` containing the sequence elements with primitives boxed.

items.issue: All ten added class comments say the conversion returns a wrapper/view, but every delegated `AsJavaConverters` method returns `null` when its receiver is explicitly `null`. This is a material result case absent from the new documentation.
items.suggestion: State that an explicitly null receiver produces null, and qualify the wrapper/view guarantees as applying to non-null receivers.

items.issue: All ten added class comments omit that the delegated `AsScalaConverters` methods return `null` for an explicitly null receiver; their unconditional wrapper/view wording is therefore false in that case.
items.suggestion: Document the null result for an explicitly null receiver and limit wrapper/view claims to non-null inputs.

items.issue: The comment says the result is always a new wrapper, but a null receiver produces null. It also omits that the map exposes only the `Properties` object's own entries, does not consult defaults, and assumes entries have String keys and values; non-String entries can fail during map operations.
items.suggestion: Document null behavior and the own-entry/String-only limitations (including that defaults are not represented by the map view).

items.issue: Claims that `ConcurrentMap.computeIfAbsent` is atomic “per the ConcurrentMap contract”. That contract does not guarantee atomicity for its default method; an arbitrary wrapped `ConcurrentMap` may use it. The implementation simply delegates to that method.
items.suggestion: Remove the atomicity claim and state that concurrency semantics are those of the wrapped map's `computeIfAbsent` implementation.

items.issue: Claims that `ConcurrentMap.compute` is atomic “per the ConcurrentMap contract”, but the contract does not guarantee atomicity for the default method used by arbitrary `ConcurrentMap` implementations.
items.suggestion: Remove the atomicity claim and document delegation to the wrapped map's `compute`, with its implementation-defined concurrency guarantees.

items.issue: The Boolean return value is described but lacks an `@return` tag even though the description does not open with “Returns”.
items.suggestion: Add `@return true`.

items.issue: The returned buffer is described but lacks an `@return` tag, and the description does not open with “Returns”.
items.suggestion: Add `@return this buffer`.

items.issue: The returned removed element is described but lacks an `@return` tag, and the description does not open with “Returns”.
items.suggestion: Add `@return the removed element`.

items.issue: The Boolean return value is described but lacks an `@return` tag, and the description does not open with “Returns”.
items.suggestion: Add `@return true` if the element was not already present, otherwise `false`.

items.issue: The Boolean return value is described but lacks an `@return` tag, and the description does not open with “Returns”.
items.suggestion: Add `@return true` if the element was present, otherwise `false`.

items.issue: The Boolean return value is described in prose but lacks an `@return` tag, and the description does not open with “Returns”.
items.suggestion: Add `@return true` if the entry was removed, otherwise `false`.

items.issue: The Boolean return value is described in prose but lacks an `@return` tag, and the description does not open with “Returns”.
items.suggestion: Add `@return true` if the value was replaced, otherwise `false`.

items.issue: The added `@note NEEDS-HUMAN` leaves an unresolved question: why is this evidence typed for `IntAccumulator` while it reuses `longAccumulatorFactoryInfo`, whose companion is `LongAccumulator`?
items.suggestion: Have a maintainer resolve the intended target type and remove the NEEDS-HUMAN note; make any code correction separately if required.

items.issue: The added `@note NEEDS-HUMAN` leaves an unresolved question: why is this evidence typed for `IntAccumulator` while it reuses `doubleAccumulatorFactoryInfo`, whose companion is `DoubleAccumulator`?
items.suggestion: Have a maintainer resolve the intended target type and remove the NEEDS-HUMAN note; make any code correction separately if required.

items.issue: The added `@note NEEDS-HUMAN` leaves unresolved whether splitting while `found` is true and `half` remains in the cached words leaves the original stepper with stale state after its superclass advances `i0` to `half`.
items.suggestion: Have a maintainer establish the state invariant and either correct the implementation in a separate change or remove the note after confirming it is safe.

items.issue: The non-Unit method’s description begins with “Creates” but omits `@return`, contrary to the documented return-tag convention. The same issue is repeated by the primitive variants.
items.suggestion: Add `@return a stepper over the prefix `[i0, half)``, or reword the summary to begin with “Returns” and state the complete return value, for all three `semiclone` methods.

items.issue: `2^30^` has an extraneous trailing caret and is not a clear code or mathematical literal in Scaladoc.

bonus_findings.issue: The pre-existing calculation can overflow `Int` subtraction and return an incorrect non-negative known size for a range with more than `Int.MaxValue` remaining elements.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Calculate the distance in `Long` and return `-1` when the remaining size cannot be represented as `Int`.

bonus_findings.issue: The pre-existing `step * n` multiplication overflows as `Int` before conversion to `Long`, so `drop` can move the iterator to an incorrect value.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Use `step.toLong * n` before adding it to `_next.toLong`.

bonus_findings.issue: Pre-existing Scaladoc says `asJavaCollection` converts a Scala `Iterator`, but its receiver and implementation convert a Scala `Iterable`.
